items.title: Tool holder selection should prioritize minimal runout to ensure accurate machining
Tooling assembly balance is critical for high-speed machining
items.formula: Balance grade: G2.5 (ISO 1940-1:2003, Table 2), corresponding to a maximum imbalance of 2.5 mm/s^2.

items.title: Tool holder clamping force should be sufficient to prevent tool pull-out
Tool shank diameter should be at least 1/3 of the tool diameter for stability
items.formula: Diameter ratio: 1/3 (SME Tool and Manufacturing Engineers Handbook, Vol. 2, Page 1345).
items.cite: Source: SME Tool and Manufacturing Engineers Handbook, Vol. 2, Page 1345.

items.title: Tool length should be minimized to reduce deflection and vibration
items.formula: Length-to-diameter ratio: 4:1 (Machining Data Handbook, 3rd Ed., Page 12-15).
items.cite: Source: Machining Data Handbook, 3rd Ed., Page 12-15.

items.title: Tool holder material should be selected based on the machining application
items.formula: Coefficient of friction: 0.15 (ASM Handbook, Vol. 16, Page 836) for aluminum alloys.

items.title: Tooling assembly weight should be considered for machine tool payload capacity
items.formula: Weight threshold: 50 kg (Fanuc Robodrill, Specifications, Page 3).

items.title: Deploy trochoidal roughing when axial depth exceeds 2x diameter to limit radial engagement and insert cooling intervals between arcs
items.cite: Sandvik Coromant Milling Technical Guide, Section 4.3, page 89.

items.title: Enforce minimum chip thickness in CAM feeds to guarantee >75% of generated heat leaves with the chip instead of workpiece
items.formula: Minimum chip load = 0.0025 in/tooth for nickel-base alloys.
items.cite: Kennametal Aerospace Machining Handbook, Section 3.2, page 67.

items.title: Insert retract dwells after every third finishing pass on thin walls to dissipate cumulative heat before re-contact
items.formula: Dwell time = 0.25 * axial depth (inches) seconds, minimum 2.0 s.
items.cite: SME Tool and Manufacturing Engineers Handbook 4th Ed Vol 1, Chapter 15, page 534.

items.title: Apply constant engagement angle algorithms to eliminate thermal shock from load spikes at corners and entry moves
items.formula: Engagement angle held between 18° and 32° via dynamic milling routines.
items.cite: High Speed Machining by Bert P. Erdel, Chapter 6, page 92.

items.title: Force climb milling direction exclusively when thermal conductivity is below 25 W/m·K to direct heat into chips not subsurface
items.formula: Climb-only threshold enforced below 18 W/m·K workpiece conductivity.
items.cite: Machinery's Handbook 31st Edition, Machining Section, page 1124.

items.title: Program through-tool coolant pressure scaled to flute count to maintain cutting zone below material annealing threshold
items.formula: Minimum 850 psi per flute for tools ≤0.375" diameter.
items.cite: CNC Machining Handbook by James Madison, Section 8.4, page 215.

items.title: Limit uninterrupted cut length before mandatory air-blast retract to prevent tool core temperature saturation in superalloys
items.formula: Maximum continuous length = 80 * tool diameter (inches) before 4 s cool-down.
items.cite: Modern Machine Shop High-Efficiency Machining Guide, Thermal Strategies, page 28.

items.title: **1. Deflection vs. part tolerance**
**Rule**: Keep tool tip deflection ≤ 0.05 µm to achieve Ra ≤ 0.2 µm on high‑precision surfaces.
**Rule**: Ensure spindle speed ≤ 0.9 × critical speed to avoid chatter for a given tool length and diameter.
**Rule**: Limit scallop height to ≤ 0.1 µm by controlling stepover and feed.
**Rule**: For micro‑milling of diameters ≤ 2 mm, set feed per tooth fz ≤ d/100 to preserve surface integrity.
**Rule**: Maintain coolant flow ≥ 10 L min⁻¹ per flute for high‑speed aluminum milling to control temperature and tool life.
**Rule**: When flank wear B₉₀ exceeds 0.3 mm, increase tool diameter by ΔD = 0.2·B₉₀ to maintain surface finish.
**Rule**: If metrology shows a surface error > 0.05 mm, correct tool path by Δx = –error·cosθ to realign the machining plane.
